newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 20.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* The Nasdaq composite closed down 20.05 at 1249.29, as technology stocks tumbled again.
* Liggett Group has offered to put a warning label on its cigarettes that "smoking is addictive" in settlement talks with state and plaintiffs' lawyers.
* AMR's American Airlines and negotiators from its pilots union reached a tentative pact on a new contract.
* Many states are reaching the limit on incentives they are willing to pay to attract small businesses.
* February's consumer price index rose a mild 0.3 percent.
* Sprint tried to play down a report Cable & Wireless might make a bid for the firm, though the chairman said he would consider more alliances if they fit company strategy.
* Delta is expected to announce a long-term exclusive aircraft supply pact with Boeing today.
* Krupp and Thyssen agreed to discuss a merger of their steel operations after Krupp said it would drop an unsolicited bid for Thyssen.
* Motorola new top management is entering the smart card business as its first major initiative.
* LVMH dropped efforts to buy a 38.75 percent stake in DFS, a duty-free retailer, from Robert Miller.
* IBM appointed its computer-services chief Dennis Welsh to the highest post after chief executive.
* R&R Donnelly named Emerson Electric executive William Davis chairman and CEO of the commercial printer.
* ConAgra agreed to pay criminal penalties of $8.3 million to settle wire fraud charges and allegations it misgraded crops and added water to make grain heavier.
* Time Magazine filed suit against CompuServe, alleging CompuServe tried to break a commitment over an electronic newsstand.
* Surveys show construction and manufacturing executives see upturns in their businesses over the next three months.
* New York State announced plans for a partial state takeover of Long Island Lighting, agreeing to buy part of Lilco for $2.5 billion plus $3.6 billion in assumed debt.
* New York Times Co plans to sell off all its magazine operations except for its golf publications.

* Heard on the Street: The rapidly unfolding deregulation and consolidation of the utlitly industry is spawning a profusion of takeover deals among retail, wholesale, regional and national power providers.

* Bonds lost ground yesterday, with the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond crossing the 7 pecent mark in intraday trading for the second consecutive day, as newly released data on inflation disappointed investors.
